Also, note that if you have gotten the answer to the question, you should call the "answer_action" tool instead of simply writing your answer in your response.

Now, I will start a new problem in a new OS. My problem is:

1. Create a folder named "temp_workspace" and capture a snapshot of the current system environment (including PATH and relevant shell variables) to "temp_workspace/env_snapshot.txt".
2. Locate all filesystem entries that could correspond to an executable named "npm" within standard binary locations and record their absolute paths to "temp_workspace/candidates.txt".
3. For each path in "temp_workspace/candidates.txt", collect and save metadata — presence, accessibility/executable status, file type, and any short version or identification output if retrievable — into "temp_workspace/candidates_metadata.txt".
4. Consolidate the findings into "temp_workspace/check_ready.txt", writing a one-line existence flag indicating whether any candidate passed the metadata/accessibility checks and including references to the detailed files to prepare for the final yes/no determination.

Tell me whether npm is installed or not. If it is installed, return 'yes'. If it is not installed, return 'no'

arguments:
{"script":"mkdir -p temp_workspace
# capture environment (PATH and shell variables included)
(env; echo; set) > temp_workspace/env_snapshot.txt 2>/dev/null

candidates_file=temp_workspace/candidates.txt
: > "$candidates_file"

# check directories from PATH
OLDIFS=$IFS; IFS=':'
for d in $PATH; do
  [ -n "$d" ] || continue
  if [ -e "$d/npm" ]; then readlink -f "$d/npm" >> "$candidates_file" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
done
IFS=$OLDIFS

# check common binary locations
for d in /bin /usr/bin /usr/local/bin /usr/sbin /sbin /opt/*/bin; do
  if [ -e "$d/npm" ]; then readlink -f "$d/npm" >> "$candidates_file" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
done

# dedupe
if [ -s "$candidates_file" ]; then sort -u -o "$candidates_file" "$candidates_file" 2>/dev/null || true; fi

meta_file=temp_workspace/candidates_metadata.txt
: > "$meta_file"
found_exec=0

if [ -s "$candidates_file" ]; then
  while IFS= read -r p; do
    [ -z "$p" ] && continue
    echo "Path: $p" >> "$meta_file"
    if [ -e "$p" ]; then echo "Exists: yes" >> "$meta_file"; else echo "Exists: no" >> "$meta_file"; fi
    if [ -x "$p" ]; then echo "Executable: yes" >> "$meta_file"; else echo "Executable: no" >> "$meta_file"; fi
    file -L "$p" 2>/dev/null | sed -e "s/^/FileType: /" >> "$meta_file" 2>/dev/null || true
    # try common version flags with timeout
    ver=""
    ver=$(timeout 2 "$p" --version 2>&1 || true)
    if [ -z "$ver" ]; then ver=$(timeout 2 "$p" -v 2>&1 || true); fi
    if [ -n "$ver" ]; then printf '%s\n' "VersionOutput: $(echo "$ver" | head -n1)" >> "$meta_file"; fi
    echo "---" >> "$meta_file"
    if [ -x "$p" ]; then found_exec=1; fi
  done < "$candidates_file"
fi

check_file=temp_workspace/check_ready.txt
if [ "$found_exec" -eq 1 ]; then
  echo "FOUND=yes;FILES=temp_workspace/candidates.txt,temp_workspace/candidates_metadata.txt,temp_workspace/env_snapshot.txt" > "$check_file"
  echo yes
else
  echo "FOUND=no;FILES=temp_workspace/candidates.txt,temp_workspace/candidates_metadata.txt,temp_workspace/env_snapshot.txt" > "$check_file"
  echo no
fi
"}
